page: Amazon Web Services m5zn.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance configuration powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom Intel Xeon 8252C processors operating at a sustained clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 24 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of system memory per vCPU. Local physical storage is omitted entirely, necessitating external Amazon Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 10 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and no GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the characteristics of this high-frequency architecture. Single-threaded performance tests demonstrate solid execution capability, with single-threaded gzip compression registering 31.88 GB/sec in the top quartile of evaluated instances. The system produced a Geekbench single-core score of 1565.0 and multi-core score of 5869.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 11012.22 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 9854.71. Memory bandwidth tests produced 54.44 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 40.64 GB/sec for large block writes. In application-level benchmarks, Redis achieved 9.28 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 7.69 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranked in the bottom quartile at 36.06 GB/sec, and CPU-based LLM inference demonstrated steep drop-offs on medium 7B models, generating only 7.44 tokens per second.

From a resource allocation perspective, the m5zn.2xlarge prioritizes per-core processing speed within a balanced compute-to-memory footprint. The high base frequency offers an advantage for applications constrained by single-thread execution latency rather than massive parallel core counts, avoiding the requirement to scale to higher tier sizes solely for clock speed. The absence of bundled local NVMe storage serves as an architectural tradeoff, increasing dependence on network storage latency and EBS bandwidth allocations. The server is well matched for gaming infrastructure, software compilation pipelines, static web serving nodes, and relational database hosting requiring balanced memory capacity alongside fast individual core processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m5zn.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance designed around high-frequency Intel Xeon 8252C processors operating at 4.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores alongside 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Network connectivity provides a 10 Gbps baseline, though the instance omits bundled local storage, requiring network-attached volumes for persistent data. Vector instruction support includes AVX, AVX-512, and AVX-512 VNNI. Benchmarks show competitive single-thread capability, led by strong single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 31.88 GB/sec and steady Redis SET throughput of 9.28 million operations per second. Multi-threaded decompression and medium-tier language model inference exhibit moderate to weak relative throughput. The configuration provides balanced resource density suitable for workloads benefiting from high clock speeds, such as build compilation, dedicated game hosting, web servers, and mid-sized databases.
